root_cause_label: Wrong Problem Formulation (Distribution-Matching Synthetic Sampling Instead of Constrained Matrix Completion via Low-Rank/Nuclear-Norm Minimization) + Superficial Self-Validation (Checks only marginal stats, not observed-entry constraints)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The model adopts an incorrect strategy by treating the task as distribution-matching synthetic sampling rather than constrained matrix completion, and the agent reinforces the failure by validating only marginal statistics instead of checking observed-entry constraints.
t_err_evidence: At step 5, the agent writes generate_synthetic_data.py which samples values from a clipped normal distribution and samples row/col indices from empirical marginal distributions, then fills a 200x200 matrix with these randomly placed entries. This ignores the essential constraint X[row_idx_i[k], col_idx_i[k]] == observed_vals_i[k] for every observed entry k in each trial i, and completely ignores the low-rank objective required by the benchmark.
t_commit_evidence: The wrong method is fully baked into the script written at step 5. All subsequent steps (6-13) either install dependencies, execute this same wrong script, or validate its outputs using wrong criteria. No step revises or reconsiders the core approach; the outcome is locked in once the script is written.
trigger_explanation: The agent proceeds on the unverified false assumption that the task requires generating new synthetic data with similar distributional properties (mean, std, sparsity), rather than reading the task specification carefully enough to understand it requires matrix completion: reconstructing a full low-rank matrix that is consistent with the provided observed entries at exactly the specified (row, col) positions.
fabrication_evidence: At step 8, the script successfully generates 20 solution files (/app/solution_0.txt through /app/solution_19.txt) that appear to be valid matrix completions but are actually randomly-sampled matrices derived from marginal distributions. The outputs do not satisfy the per-instance observed-entry equality constraints (X[row_i[k], col_i[k]] == observed_vals_i[k]) and are not low-rank. The agent then runs a validation script (steps 11-12) that prints 'Validation completed. Synthetic data closely resembles original data!' based only on aggregate mean/std/sparsity checks, and at step 13 declares the task complete, fabricating a successful outcome.
